jobs.title: Natividad Hospital Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Natividad is a county-owned and operated public health care system and Level II Trauma Center serving the diverse communities of Monterey County. Located in Salinas, California, Natividad provides comprehensive inpatient, outpatient, emergency, diagnostic and specialty care to adults and children, regardless of their ability to pay or immigration status.

Founded in 1886, Natividad has served Monterey County for 140 years and remains one of the region’s most important public institutions. The 172-bed hospital is supported by nearly 1,700 employees and more than 400 physicians and medical staff. Each year, Natividad records approximately 60,000 emergency department visits, more than 11,000 inpatient admissions and nearly 2,200 births.

Natividad is fully accredited by The Joint Commission and is one of California’s 17 public health care systems. It serves as Monterey County’s essential safety net hospital, its only teaching hospital and one of the Central Coast’s most important providers of advanced and lifesaving care.

The hospital operates the only Level II Trauma Center in Monterey County, providing 24-hour access to trauma-specialized care and treating approximately 1,400 trauma patients annually. Natividad also offers nationally recognized women’s and children’s services, a Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit affiliated with UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospitals, acute rehabilitation, behavioral health, surgical and specialty care, comprehensive primary care and Monterey County’s only child maltreatment clinic.

Natividad’s longstanding academic affiliation with the University of California, San Francisco is central to its mission. Its nationally recognized UCSF-affiliated Family Medicine Residency is one of the university’s original affiliate residency programs and prepares physicians to serve medically underserved communities, advance health equity and become leaders in family medicine.

Natividad is owned and operated by County of Monterey and governed by the County of Monterey Board of Supervisors, with guidance from a Board of Trustees. The Hospital Chief Executive Officer reports directly to the Board of Supervisors and works closely with the Board of Trustees, county leadership, elected officials, labor representatives, community partners and other stakeholders. The CEO will lead an executive team that includes the Chief Medical Officer, Chief Nursing Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Information Officer and Assistant Hospital Administrators.

The incoming CEO will inherit a highly regarded public hospital with a strong financial foundation, a committed workforce and a culture deeply rooted in quality, compassion and service. This is not a mandate to redefine Natividad’s identity. Rather, the next CEO will maintain and enhance the organization’s strengths while positioning it to respond to a rapidly changing health care, financial and political environment.

The CEO will provide strategic, operational and financial leadership for the hospital and will be responsible for advancing high-quality patient care, long-term sustainability, workforce engagement, regulatory compliance and community impact. The successful candidate will balance fiscal discipline with thoughtful investment, identify opportunities to responsibly grow the organization’s reach and strengthen Natividad’s position as a trusted provider of choice throughout Monterey County.

This role requires a politically astute and highly collaborative executive who can operate effectively within a visible public-sector governance structure. The CEO must be comfortable working across two boards and building trusted relationships with county officials, legislators, medical staff, employees, organized labor, community leaders, donors and regional health care partners. The successful candidate will be credible in the boardroom, effective in the community and able to communicate clearly in an environment where decisions are subject to public scrutiny.

The Board is seeking a forward-looking leader who can translate vision into action and bring stakeholders together around meaningful change. The next CEO will have the opportunity to advance the patient experience, strengthen access and care coordination, support strategic investments in technology and facilities, attract and develop clinical talent, deepen educational and community partnerships and elevate awareness of Natividad’s clinical quality and distinctive public mission.

The successful candidate will believe deeply in the population Natividad serves. Monterey County is culturally, economically and linguistically diverse and includes a large agricultural workforce, rural communities, Indigenous-language speakers and residents who face significant barriers to care. More than half of Natividad’s patients are covered by Medi-Cal. The needs of this community must remain at the center of the organization’s strategy and every major decision.

Candidates should bring at least five years of increasingly responsible health care or hospital administration experience, including three years in a Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer or comparable executive-level role. The successful candidate will have demonstrated experience leading a complex acute care hospital or health system and a strong understanding of hospital operations, finance, clinical services, medical staff relations, regulatory requirements and workforce leadership.

Experience in a public hospital, safety net health system, county-operated organization or similarly complex and politically governed environment is strongly preferred. Candidates should possess the financial acumen to evaluate operating and capital priorities, understand payer and reimbursement dynamics and ensure the organization’s continued long-term sustainability. They must also demonstrate the ability to work constructively with organized labor and to build alignment across stakeholders with differing perspectives and priorities.

The ideal candidate will be an innovative, mission-driven and emotionally intelligent leader with exceptional judgment, integrity and communication skills. This executive will be visible, accessible and collaborative, while also possessing the courage to make difficult decisions and challenge established practices when necessary. Experience working with culturally and economically diverse communities and a genuine commitment to health equity and public service will be essential.

A master’s degree from an accredited college or university in Hospital Administration, Health Care Administration, Business Administration, Public Health, Nursing or a closely related field is expected. Candidates may alternatively possess a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree from an accredited school of medicine. Equivalent combinations of education, training and experience that demonstrate the required qualifications will also be considered.

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead an organization with a strong foundation, a distinctive mission and a vital role in the future health of Monterey County.

Application Information

Review of candidate materials will begin immediately, and the ability to apply or nominate will continue until the position has been filled. The complete position profile can be found at: Natividad Hospital Position Profile Summer 2026. Applications should include a cover letter and résumé and may be submitted at: caldwell.thriveapp.ly/job/1317

The County of Monterey has retained Caldwell Partners, an executive search firm, to assist with this search. Confidential inquiries, nominations and referrals may be directed to: NatividadCEO@caldwell.com

Compensation

The current salary range for this position is $439,452 to $599,869 annually. The final compensation package will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, education, skills and organizational needs.

Please note that the classification is currently undergoing a salary review by the County of Monterey and will be communicated as the search progresses.

The successful candidate will be required to complete a background check, possess a valid California Class C driver’s license or provide approved transportation, and be available to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, holidays and during emergencies.

Executive Summary

Contra Costa Health (CCH) is seeking an exceptional executive leader to serve as its inaugural Chief Operating Officer (COO), a newly created position designed to modernize one of California’s largest and most comprehensive integrated public health systems.

The COO will help shape the future of a healthcare system that uniquely combines a health plan, a public hospital, community health centers, behavioral health services, public health, housing and homelessness services, and community health and safety programs under one integrated organization.

As the County’s primary Medi-Cal provider, Contra Costa Health touches the lives of a significant portion of the County’s 1.2M residents. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to improve access, quality, efficiency, and health outcomes for some of California’s most vulnerable populations while helping lead the organization through one of the most transformational periods in its history.

About Contra Costa Health

Contra Costa Health is one of the most comprehensive county health systems in the United States.

Serving one of the Country’s largest and most diverse counties, the department integrates:

Contra Costa Regional Medical Center and Health Centers – A county-operated public hospital and network of nine primary care health centers
Contra Costa Health Plan
Behavioral Health Services
Public Health
Health, Housing and Homelessness
Community Health and Safety

Together these services create an integrated delivery system that allows Contra Costa Health to influence both how care is delivered and how it is financed—an uncommon model that enables innovation, flexibility, and system-wide coordination.

The department oversees approximately 5,000 employees and operates with an annual budget approaching $4B.

To learn more about Contra Costa Health, check out their website: cchealth.org

The Position

Reporting directly to the Director of Health Services, the Chief Operating Officer serves as a key member of the department’s executive team and works collaboratively to develop strategy, align resources, and enhance organizational effectiveness across Contra Costa Health.

Leading operational strategy and providing direct oversight for major divisions in Contra Costa Health, including Contra Costa Regional Medical Center, affiliated Health Centers, Contra Costa Health Plan, Behavioral Health, and Community Health and Safety divisions such as Public Health and Health, Housing and Homelessness.

Primary Responsibilities Include

Serves as the Director of Health Services’ designee in their absence, ensuring continuity of executive leadership, decision-making, and operational performance
Plans, develops, and implements long-term system objectives, including modernization initiatives, service expansion, and strategies to support sustainable organizational growth
Oversee department-wide operations to improve transparency, reduce duplication, increase efficiency, and implement consistent standards and best practices across the organization
Develops and maintains collaborative working relationships with other County departments to strengthen coordination, promote innovation, and optimize service delivery
Leads the adaptation of organizational systems and operations to effectively respond to evolving healthcare delivery models, financing structures, and managed care environments
Collaborates with the CCH Chief Financial Officer in the financial management of CCH, including long-term budget planning and alignment of operational and fiscal strategy
Provides oversight to Deputy Directors across all CCH divisions, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and performance standards
Oversee executive responses to regulatory and inspection findings, ensuring compliance, accountability, and continuous improvement across the health system

The Ideal Candidate

Contra Costa Health seeks an accomplished executive with operational expertise, leadership presence, and strategic mindset to lead a highly complex public healthcare organization through transformational change.

The Successful Candidate Will Bring

Executive Healthcare Operations Experience

Extensive executive leadership within large, complex healthcare organizations
Experience overseeing operations for hospitals, integrated delivery systems, health systems, or large ambulatory networks
Demonstrated success leading largescale and complex operational transformation and performance improvement
Experience aligning clinical operations with financial sustainability
Experience working in a unionized environment

Strategic Leadership

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

Strong operational leadership expertise
Excellent relationship-building skills
Political awareness and sound judgment
Data-driven decision making
Commitment to accountability and continuous improvement

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Education:
Possession of a master’s degree from an accredited college or university in public health, hospital or healthcare administration, business or public administration, social or behavioral sciences, health sciences, social work, or a closely related field.

Experience:
Seven (7) years of full-time (or equivalent) progressively responsible professional management experience within a healthcare or human services organization. This experience must include at least three (3) years in an executive-level leadership role within a large, complex, and diverse public or nonprofit organization providing health or human services.

Selection Process

Candidates are encouraged to express interest early in the recruitment process. This position will remain open until filled. For first consideration, please submit your application by September 7th, 2026.

Applications should be submitted through Contra Costa County.

Director of Development for Athletics

It is an exciting time to join Sonoma State University as we launch the Director of Development for Athletics search! Sonoma State University is seeking a highly motivated, relationship-driven individual who will serve as a vital component of the educational experience at Sonoma State, emphasizing the importance of academic achievement alongside athletic success. In fall 2027, Sonoma State Athletics will have 10 NCAA Division II teams competing in the California Collegiate Athletic Association conference as part of the broader reimagining of the university and its programs. Seawolf Athletics represents an exciting investment in student life, campus pride, and the future of Sonoma State. This position will have the unique opportunity during this monumental time to manage and cultivate a portfolio of major gift prospects and fundraising efforts to support the Intercollegiate Athletics Program and future programming efforts. The ideal candidate in this role should have a positive attitude, an active, energetic mind, and a leadership style that is characterized by highly ethical practices and a commitment to inclusivity, openness, flexibility, integrity, and kindness.

About Us

Sonoma State's Intercollegiate Athletics Program is committed to providing quality experience for all student-athletes, focusing on fair play, sportsmanship, and teamwork. It also aims to enhance the University's mission by fostering pride and involvement among students, faculty, staff, alumni, and community members. We are committed to achieving excellence through teaching, scholarship, learning and inclusion. In line with our Strategic Plan and our Seawolf Commitment, the University values include diversity, sustainability, community engagement, respect, responsibility, excellence and integrity. We strive to cultivate a community in which a diverse population can learn and work in an atmosphere of civility and respect. We encourage innovation, experimentation and creativity, as well as contributions to equity and inclusion, in the pursuit of excellence for all members of our university community.

The Role

Reporting to the Associate Vice President of Development, working in concert with the Interim Director of Athletics, and the President, the Director of Development for Athletics establishes fundraising strategies and directs and conducts fundraising activities to secure philanthropic support for the Intercollegiate Athletics Program in alignment with Sonoma State University priorities. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, identifying, qualifying, cultivating and soliciting potential donors for the Athletics Program; organizing and providing effective communication with donors and potential donors; stewarding alumni and other individual prospects, sponsors and major donors; coordinating gift processing; recruiting, training and motivating volunteers for the university; and, other fundraising projects.

Qualifications

This position requires a minimum of four years of experience in successful relationship building with prospects, volunteers, and board members, along with a demonstrated aptitude to be successful in face-to-face fundraising, including 4 years of progressively responsible and applicable management and/or supervisory experience. Bachelor's degree required. The incumbent must have a proven track record of successfully working with individual donors, soliciting and securing gifts and demonstrate experience in designing and implementing successful fundraising strategies. Experience in athletic fundraising within a university environment and a strong understanding of university culture and corporate partnerships highly preferred. Please review the position description for full scope of responsibilities and qualifications.

Application Deadline

This position is open until filled. For full consideration, please submit an application, resume and cover letter addressing the prompt below by 8am on Tuesday, August 11th.

Prompt:
Please describe your experience designing and implementing a comprehensive development plan for an organization, agency, or project. In addition, please describe how your qualifications and experience would directly translate to this role and support the future of fundraising for Athletics.

Salary And Benefits

Starting salary placement depends on qualifications and experience and is anticipated to be in the range of $8,334 - $8,667 a month. This position is a member of the Management Personnel Plan and serves at the pleasure of the President. This position is eligible for a broad range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurances, retirement (CalPERS), tuition waiver, vacation and sick leave. In addition, 15 paid holidays are offered each year. Sonoma State University is also a Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF) Employer (comprehensive benefits summary PDF).

The Opportunity

Westmark School—a nationally recognized leader in educating students with language-based learning differences—seeks an entrepreneurial, relationship-driven leader to serve as its Director of Development and Strategic Partnerships. This is a pivotal new role designed to expand Westmark’s philanthropic reach, deepen engagement with mission-aligned external partners, and strengthen the School’s long-term sustainability.

A central responsibility of the Director is to strategically support the Head of School and the Board of Trustees in all aspects of major gifts fundraising. The Director will cultivate and steward relationships with Westmark’s closest constituents—including current parents, grandparents, alumni families, and former trustees—who have the capacity to make leadership gifts of $100,000 and above.

The Director will ensure that the Westmark Fund and Spring Gala meet operating budget goals and that teams of volunteers are actively engaged in the execution of these annual fundraising initiatives.

At The Same Time, The Director Will Broaden Westmark’s Visibility And Impact By Identifying And Securing New Sources Of External Support, Including

Individual philanthropists beyond the immediate School community
Corporate partnerships
Foundation relationships
Mission-aligned organizations in education, neurodiversity, technology, and workforce development

The Director of Development and Strategic Partnerships reports directly to the Head of School and serves as a key member of the senior leadership team.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to sit in on meetings and work on a computer for long periods of time; and is occasionally required to walk, reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, talk, and hear. Westmark seeks a candidate who is both a strategic thinker and a hands-on relationship builder—someone energized by the opportunity to shape and expand the School’s philanthropic reach.

The ideal candidate will bring a blend of major gifts expertise, partnership development experience, and leadership presence required to work closely with the Head of School, Board of Trustees, and senior administrators.

The ability to translate institutional priorities—especially the 2026–2029 strategic plan—into a clear, actionable roadmap for philanthropy and partnerships.
A growth mindset and entrepreneurial approach to identifying new funding opportunities, building pipelines, and expanding Westmark’s visibility beyond its immediate community.

Exceptional interpersonal skills and the ability to inspire trust, credibility, and enthusiasm among donors, volunteers, corporate partners, and colleagues.

Skill in creating clear roles, timelines, and tools that enable effective peer-to-peer outreach.

Experience developing multi-layered corporate relationships that may include philanthropy, sponsorships, employee engagement, or workforce-readiness initiatives.
Strong grant-writing skills, including the ability to craft compelling narratives, manage deadlines, and steward institutional funders.
An understanding of trends in DEI and corporate philanthropy—particularly as they relate to neurodiversity, education, and talent development.

Strong organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work on tight timelines.
Comfort with prospect management systems, dashboards, and data analysis to inform strategy and track progress.
A commitment to best practices in donor stewardship, compliance, and ethical fundraising.

Mission Alignment and Cultural Competence

A deep appreciation for Westmark School’s mission, vision, and the strengths of neurodiverse learners.
The ability to communicate the School’s impact with authenticity, clarity, and emotional intelligence.
Cultural humility and the ability to engage respectfully with families, students, and partners from diverse backgrounds.

Director of Advancement

PS1 Pluralistic School | Santa Monica, California

About The Role

At PS1, we believe that impactful schools change lives and that strong communities make those impactful schools possible. Ours is a community where children are deeply known, families feel a true sense of belonging, and learning is rooted in curiosity, equity, and joy.

A thriving independent school is built at the intersection of educational excellence, financial sustainability, and community connection. The Director of Advancement plays a central role in sustaining and growing that intersection, responsible for cultivating the relationships, resources, and shared sense of purpose that advance the school’s mission within the broader circle of our community of supporters.

Reporting to the Head of School and serving on the Senior Administrative Team, this role leads the school’s fundraising, alumni relations, and capital campaign efforts. The Director of Advancement stewards projects that enhance the mission of the school, describes the benefits these projects will have for our students, and secures the financial capital to bring such projects to fruition.

Guided by our vision, Many voices build a better world , the Director of Advancement ensures that the school can continue to provide progressive education that sparks curious and critical thinkers, fosters socio-economic diversity, and builds a pluralistic, mission-driven community. This role combines strategic vision, relational leadership, operational excellence, and a strong presence on campus.

At PS1, advancement is storytelling.

This role is about translating the magic of classrooms and community into lasting relationships and mission-aligned investment, ensuring that:

Families feel connected to something meaningful
Alumni remember and feel reconnected
Donors see the real impact of their philanthropy

This position calls for a strategic, relational leader who can hold both long-term vision and near-term execution, who understands that philanthropy is rooted in trust and shared purpose, who is interested in building relationships with children and valuing their growing voice, and who is energized by growth, change, and possibility in a pluralistic community.

Core Responsibilities

Advancement Strategy & Institutional Leadership

Develop and implement a comprehensive, mission-aligned advancement strategy encompassing alumni and grandparent relations, the Annual Fund, major and planned giving, and a future capital campaign, work in collaboration with the Parents Guild and school team to plan and execute the spring fundraising Gala
Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Head of School and Board Advancement Committee, providing data-driven insights to inform philanthropic strategy and institutional priorities
Actively participate on the Senior Administrative Team, bringing an advancement lens to school-wide planning, resource allocation, and community engagement

Alumni Relations & Community Stewardship

Build and strengthen lifelong alumni relationships rooted in belonging, engagement, and shared mission
Design inclusive programming and communication that reflects the school’s values of pluralism, community, and educational excellence
Partner closely with the Director of Student & Community Life to align alumni engagement with student life initiatives and broader community-building efforts

Annual Fund & Impact Communication

Lead the Annual Fund, articulating its impact on the school’s programs, student experiences, and tuition assistance initiatives
Translate classroom and programmatic outcomes into compelling stories that inspire participation and giving
Steward donors with care through recognition events, communications, and ongoing relationship-building
Build a culture of philanthropy rooted in shared responsibility, access, and community investment
Partner with Director of Communications and Marketing to publish an annual Report on Philanthropy

Major Gifts & Planned Giving

Develop and sustain a robust major and planned giving program, identifying and cultivating donors in collaboration with the Head of School and Board volunteers
Partner with key volunteers to ensure relationship-driven fundraising and stewardship that honors donors and advances the school’s mission

Capital Campaign Leadership

Lead the planning and execution of a mission-driven capital campaign to fund the development of school-owned properties in ways that expand programming, strengthen community partnerships, and further the school’s educational mission
Clearly articulate why a capital campaign is essential for the school’s future, connecting physical spaces to student experience, equity, and long-term sustainability
Manage campaign strategy, phases, feasibility studies, donor cultivation, and public engagement, ensuring alignment with mission, values, and institutional priorities
Identify and collaborate with outside resources and consultants to further mission-aligned future development and growth of the school

Operations, Data & Systems Management

Maintain fluency with fundraising database tools, Google Drive, and other digital systems to track donor engagement, giving trends, and campaign progress
Ensure that all advancement data, reports, and materials are accurate, well-organized, and accessible to the Head of School, Board, and staff as appropriate
Oversee administrative support and coordinate tasks efficiently, balancing strategic vision with operational execution

Campus Presence & Educational Fluency

Maintain a consistent, visible presence on campus, building relationships with students, faculty, and families
Observe classrooms and student life to understand and describe what is happening in the learning environment
Translate those observations into fundraising messaging that demonstrates the tangible impact of gifts on student outcomes and the overall mission
Participate in the daily life of the school; serve on committees, attend all-school events, be playful with children and colleagues, and find joy in the life of an elementary school

Collaboration & Representation

Collaborate closely with the Director of Enrollment Strategy and Director of Communications and Marketing to align clear, compelling, and values-driven strategy, messaging, and storytelling.
Serve as a visible ambassador for the school at conferences, community events, and professional gatherings
Pursue professional development in independent school advancement, philanthropy, and capital campaign best practices
Represent the school in conversations and negotiations with consultants, lawyers, vendors, and partners to strengthen the school’s position in the market and ensure the financial sustainability of its future.

Our Mission, Vision & Values in Action

We Seek a Leader Who Embodies Our Mission To Spark Curious And Critical Thinkers Who Confidently Contribute To Their Communities, And Who Lives Our Values

Learn With Joy — honoring curiosity, questions, and learning from failure
Discover Your Full Self — cultivating empathy, responsibility, and confidence
Honor Our Lived Experiences — embracing diverse identities and perspectives
Be Part of Something Bigger — building connection, purpose, and collective impact

Compensation & Benefits

This position is competitively compensated with benefits. Salary is $160,000 - $190,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Why This Role Matters

Philanthropy makes possible what tuition alone cannot.

At PS1, the Director of Development ensures that the school has the resources to invest in its people, programs, and places, expand access, and imagine its future, all while strengthening the sense of belonging that defines the community.

This role is not just about raising funds. It is about cultivating belonging, activating shared purpose, and stewarding a community’s belief in progressive education. It is an opportunity to help shape not only how a school is funded, but how it is experienced by students, families, alumni, and generations to come.

Skills, Experience & Dispositions

Demonstrated success leading alumni relations, annual giving, major gifts programs, and capital campaigns, preferably in an independent school or mission-driven organization
Relational and strategic leader able to build trust with donors, Board members, parents, alumni, and colleagues
Skilled at translating classroom experiences, student outcomes, and program impact into compelling philanthropic narratives
Strong presence on campus and comfort engaging in the life of the school
Technologically proficient using data, CRM systems, fundraising databases, Google Drive, and other digital collaboration tools
Systems-oriented, able to manage multiple priorities simultaneously, and execute projects with rigor and timeliness
Open to change, reflective, adaptable, and committed to ongoing learning and professional growth
Exceptional communication skills, including writing, public speaking, and donor presentations
Collaborative, consensus-building, and mission-aligned, with deep commitment to diversity, equity, and pluralism
Familiarity with — and personal alignment to — progressive education principles.
Warmth, flexibility, integrity, and a sense of humor.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) will be a strategic partner and the operational backbone of this consumer products company
— responsible for building and scaling a top-notch operations platform that delivers uncompromising product quality, reliability, and efficiency.

This role owns end-to-end operations, including supply and demand planning, inventory management, manufacturing partnerships, sourcing, quality, and operational readiness within our baby and maternal health categories. The COO will bring deep operational expertise and hands-on understanding of manufacturing processes, materials, and trade-offs — paired with a strong appreciation for how operational decisions directly impact product performance, brand trust, and consumer outcomes. This leader will also be open to leveraging emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools, to improve forecasting accuracy, operational efficiency, quality oversight, and speed to market.

The ideal candidate is a true operator: someone who understands how products are actually made, how supply chains really work, and how to collaborate deeply with Product Development and Marketing to ensure that products are not only scalable and profitable, but exceptional in quality, safety, and integrity. This is a hands-on executive role in a growing company: the COO must balance strategic foresight with tactical execution, operating in the details while shaping long-term growth.

End-to-End Operations Leadership

Own all aspects of operations, including supply planning, demand forecasting, manufacturing, sourcing, logistics, and fulfillment.
Design and lead an integrated demand and supply planning process across DTC, omni-channel retail, and marketplace channels.
Ensure consistent, reliable product availability while minimizing inventory risk and waste.
Establish operational rhythms, KPIs, and dashboards to track performance, risks, and opportunities.

Manufacturing & Supplier Partnerships

Lead and manage strategic relationships with manufacturers, co-packers, and key suppliers.
Bring deep understanding of manufacturing processes, materials, quality controls, and cost drivers — with particular strength or understanding in at least one of the following product categories - personal care or beauty/skincare

Evaluate and select manufacturing partners based on quality, capability, scalability, compliance, and values alignment.
Partner closely with manufacturers to drive continuous improvement, innovation, and cost efficiency without compromising quality or safety.

Product Development & Commercialization Partnership

Work hand-in-hand with Product Development and Innovation to ensure products are designed for manufacturability, scalability, and quality from the outset.
Provide operational input into materials selection, formulation, sourcing, process design.
Lead the operational readiness for new product launches — from pilot runs through full commercialization.
Serve as a critical thought partner in evaluating trade-offs between performance, materials, cost, and scalability.

Operational Intelligence & Systems

Evaluate and implement AI-enabled tools to improve demand forecasting, supply planning, inventory management, and scenario modeling.
Leverage data and automation to identify inefficiencies, reduce waste, and improve margin over time.
Partner with Finance, Product, and external technology resources to modernize operational decision-making.
Use data-driven insights to inform manufacturing, sourcing, and capacity planning decisions.
Build the operational infrastructure required to support growth — including tools, systems, and processes.

Inventory Management & Working Capital Ownership

Own end-to-end inventory strategy and execution across DTC, omni-channel retail, and marketplace channels.
Balance service levels with cash efficiency, freshness, and quality.
Define and manage inventory targets, including weeks of supply, safety stock, and reorder points by SKU and channel.
Lead cross-functional inventory reviews to align forecasting, production, and demand signals.
Partner with Finance to manage working capital, inventory turns, and obsolescence risk.
Implement tools and dashboards (including AI-enabled forecasting) to improve inventory accuracy and decision-making.

Quality, Compliance & Safety

Ensure all products meet or exceed quality, safety, regulatory, and compliance standards across categories and markets.
Build and maintain robust quality assurance and quality control processes.

Team and Cross-Functional Leadership

Lead and develop a high-performing operations team as the company scales.
Partner deeply with Marketing and Brand to ensure operational decisions support brand promises and consumer trust.
Translate marketing and growth plans into operational realities — aligning production, inventory, and logistics accordingly.
Act as a collaborative, solutions-oriented leader across teams, breaking down silos between operations, product, and marketing.

What We’re Looking For

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in operations, supply chain, or manufacturing, ideally within baby, personal care, beauty, or wellness categories.
Deep, hands-on understanding of manufacturing processes, materials, and sourcing — not just oversight.
Experience adopting or scaling systems, analytics, or automation in operations, supply chain, or manufacturing environments.
Demonstrated experience working closely with product development and marketing teams.
Proven experience managing inventory complexity across multiple channels with different service-level requirements.
Proven ability to scale operations in a growth-stage consumer business.
Strong judgment and sensitivity to product quality, safety, and consumer trust.
Comfortable navigating complexity, ambiguity, and trade-offs.
Possess creativity and flexibility needed to work in a small, entrepreneurial company.
Mission-driven leader who believes that how a product is made matters just as much as what it does.

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Enterprise Applications
jobs.description:
The New York City Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) invests in a network of community-based organizations and programs to alleviate the effects of poverty and to provide opportunities for New Yorkers and communities to flourish.

The IT Application Development Unit is looking for a Deputy Director of Enterprise Applications. The Deputy Director will report to the Chief IT Architect and will be accountable for the success of a portfolio of Intranet applications for the agency. The Deputy Director will manage a team of software developers and senior software developers providing day-to-day leadership, guidance, and mentorship.

Job Responsibilities

Translate architectural direction from the Chief IT Architect into actionable technical plans for the development team.
Lead the design and implementation of solutions using Microsoft technologies such as .NET, C#, ASP.NET Core, Azure services, SQL Server, and related frameworks.
Ensure adherence to architectural standards, coding best practices, and enterprise patterns.
Conduct technical reviews of solution designs, code, and infrastructure to maintain quality and alignment with architectural goals.
Assign tasks, manage workloads, and ensure the team meets delivery timelines.
Foster a collaborative, high-performance engineering culture focused on continuous improvement.
Support developers in resolving complex technical issues and removing blockers.
Collaborate closely with the Chief IT Architect, project managers, business analysts, and QA teams to ensure smooth delivery.
Track progress, identify risks, and communicate status updates to leadership.
Ensure solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned with business objectives.
Guide the team in building cloud-ready and cloud-native solutions using Microsoft Azure.
Oversee CI/CD pipelines, automated deployments, and environment management.
Ensure applications meet performance, scalability, and security requirements.
Enforce secure coding practices and ensure compliance with organizational and industry standards.
Oversee code reviews, technical documentation, and adherence to SDLC processes.
Ensure solutions are maintainable, scalable, and aligned with long-term architectural strategy.
Maintain clear technical documentation for systems, APIs, and architectural decisions.
Lead knowledge-sharing sessions, technical workshops, and onboarding for new team members.
Communicate complex technical concepts in a clear, business-friendly manner.
Provide input on strategic technology decisions and long-term IT roadmap planning.

Minimum Qualifications

A master's degree in computer science from an accredited college or university and three (3) years of progressively more responsible, full-time, satisfactory experience in Information Technology (IT) including applications development, systems development, data communications and networking, database administration, data processing, or user services. At least eighteen (18) months of this experience must have been in an administrative, managerial or executive capacity in the areas of applications development, systems development, data communications and networking, database administration, data processing or in the supervision of staff performing these duties; or
A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and four (4) years of progressively more responsible, full-time, satisfactory experience as described in "1" above; or
A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent, and six (6) years of progressively more responsible, full-time, satisfactory experience as described in "1" above; or
A satisfactory combination of education and experience equivalent to "1", "2" or "3" above. However, all candidates must have at least a four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent and must possess at least three (3) years of experience as described in "1" above, including the eighteen (18) months of administrative, managerial, executive or supervisory experience as described in "1" above.

In the absence of a baccalaureate degree, undergraduate credits may be substituted for a maximum of two (2) years of the required experience in IT on the basis of 30 semester credits for six (6) months of the required experience. Graduate credits in computer science may be substituted for a maximum of one (1) year of the required experience in IT on the basis of 30 graduate semester credits in computer science for one (1) year of the required IT experience. However, undergraduate and/or graduate credits may not be substituted for the eighteen (18) months of experience in an administrative, managerial, executive, or supervisory capacity as described in "1" above.

Preferred Skills

Minimum of 5 years of experience leading technical teams
Knowledge of one or more server-side programming languages (e.g., Java, C#)
Practical knowledge of the Scrum framework and Flow Metrics
Experience with using automation for continuous integration and delivery; experience with Azure DevOps is a plus
Experience writing technical documentation
Experience identifying and resolving security vulnerabilities; ISC2 certifications are a plus

Residency Requirement

New York City Residency is not required for this position

The CEO-in-Training (CIT) Program
is designed to prepare outstanding leaders for an opportunity to run one of our assisted living, independent living, or memory care communities. This salaried, full-time training program
typically lasts 3–6 months, depending on your background and experience. CITs may advance to lead one of our thriving communities or future acquisition, with continued mentorship and operational support from experienced partners.

As a CIT, you will gain hands-on practical experience in operations, clinical care, and business management under the guidance of an experienced Executive Director/CEO. Engage in immersive, on-the-job training across operational, care, and administrative functions
Shadow department heads and front-line staff to understand the day-to-day rhythm of community life

Study relevant state regulations and best practices in senior living operations

jobs.description:
The Executive Director serves as the chief executive and administrative officer of the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) and is responsible for implementing the strategic direction, policies, and priorities established by the Board of Directors.

Under the oversight of the Board, the Executive Director provides leadership for MCEC's programs, operations, financial management, external partnerships, organizational development, and personnel in support of MCEC's statutory mission to advance clean energy, energy efficiency, and related economic development in Maryland.

This position requires an executive who is equally comfortable serving as MCEC's principal external representative while leading the organization internally. The Executive Director is responsible for setting the strategic vision, building relationships with government and industry partners, developing organizational capability, leading day-to-day operations, directing department leaders, ensuring sound financial stewardship, and maintaining accountability for organizational performance.

The Executive Director must demonstrate a commitment to MCEC's mission, engage with stakeholders, and be willing to operate at both the strategic and operational levels, transitioning seamlessly between executive leadership, organizational management, and hands-on execution as organizational priorities require.

Organizational Leadership & Administration
Serve as the chief executive and administrative officer of MCEC, providing leadership for all organizational functions.
Lead, manage, coach, and develop the organization's Directors and leadership team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Provide day-to-day leadership of organizational operations, ensuring alignment between Board-approved priorities and operational execution.
Establish organizational goals, performance expectations, management systems, policies, and processes that support operational excellence.
Direct organizational planning, resource allocation, and cross-functional collaboration.
Monitor organizational performance through key performance indicators and implement improvements as necessary.
Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, policies, and ethical standards.

External Relations & Stakeholder Engagement
Serve as MCEC's primary spokesperson and representative.
Build relationships with elected officials, state agencies, local governments, utilities, capital providers, workforce organizations, academic institutions, and community partners.
Represent MCEC before legislative committees, public forums, and industry organizations.
Host major MCEC education and engagement events like the Maryland Clean Energy Summit and Legislative Reception.

Strategy Execution & Program Oversight
Develop and implement the strategic priorities approved by the Board.
Oversee the design, implementation, and performance of MCEC programs, financing initiatives, procurement support, and technical assistance offerings.
Identify emerging market opportunities, organizational risks, and strategic initiatives.
Report organizational performance and strategic progress to the Board.

Financial Stewardship & Resource Management
Oversee budgeting, financial planning, audits, grants, investments, internal controls, and financial reporting.
Ensure responsible stewardship of public funds and organizational resources.
Support long-term financial sustainability through partnerships and funding opportunities.

Board Governance & Support
Serve as the primary liaison to the Board of Directors.
Prepare Board materials, recommendations, and reports.
Implement Board directives.
Ensure compliance with Open Meetings Act, FOIA/PIA, ethics, and governance requirements.

Risk Management, Compliance & Ethics
Provide executive oversight for human resources, procurement, information technology, cybersecurity, records management, enterprise policies, and ethics compliance.
Identify and mitigate operational, financial, legal, and reputational risks.
Promote a culture of integrity, transparency, and accountability.

Qualifications & Experience
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.
Significant executive leadership and relationship building experience in clean energy, finance, public administration, economic development, government, nonprofit, or related fields. Knowledge of tech commercialization is also relevant.
Experience with stakeholder engagement, and especially State of Maryland government officials.
Demonstrated experience leading both strategic initiatives and day-to-day organizational operations.
Experience in project or structured finance, portfolio management, and public or quasi-public governance. Understanding of financial instruments used to finance clean energy projects.
Experience with Board governance, personnel leadership, budgeting, grants, procurement, and organizational development.
Event development and management experience desirable.
Excellent public presentation, written and oral communication skills.

Licenses and Certifications
Possession of a valid driver's license meeting the requirements of Maryland law, and other Maryland Clean Energy Center policies.

Physical Demands
Visual requirements for computer activities are essential. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is routinely required to talk, hear, sit, walk, bend, stoop, reach with hands and arms, and use hands and fingers.

Work Environment
The Executive Director is expected to perform responsibilities with an appropriate sense of urgency while balancing strategic leadership with active operational management. Success requires the ability to lead in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment while representing MCEC with professionalism before the Board, government officials, partners, and the public.

Salary Range

MCEC offers a competitive executive compensation package commensurate with the successful candidate's qualifications, experience, and demonstrated leadership capabilities.

The Executive Director serves as the senior leader of West Palm Beach Mobility Coalition (WPBgo), providing strategic leadership and operational oversight to advance mobility solutions, transportation demand management programs, and partnerships that improve access, reduce congestion, and support economic growth in West Palm Beach. The Executive Director is responsible for overseeing the organization’s daily operations, implementing Board directed initiatives, managing programs and partnerships, and ensuring the successful execution of WPBgo’s mission and objectives.  

The Executive Director works closely with local governments, transit agencies, employers, developers, community organizations, and funding partners to improve mobility, reduce congestion, enhance transportation accessibility, and support economic development goals.   

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership

Lead implementation of WPBgo’s strategic vision, goals, and annual business plan.  
Identify and pursue opportunities to expand transportation programs, services, partnerships, and funding sources.  
Lead long-term planning efforts to address regional mobility and transportation challenges.  
Monitor emerging transportation trends, technologies, and best practices.  

Program Management and Performance Measurement

Oversee all transportation demand management programs, commuter services, mobility initiatives, and special projects.  
Develop and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure program success, including ridership growth, employer participation, emissions reduction, and cost efficiency.  
Use data and performance results to evaluate outcomes, improve program effectiveness, strengthen accountability, and maximize return on investment.  
Ensure compliance with federal, state, regional, and local transportation regulations and funding requirements.  
Lead programs that encourage the use of sustainable transportation options, including public transit, ridesharing, walking, biking, micromobility, and employer transportation commuter benefits, to enhance mobility and reduce single occupancy vehicle trips.  

Financial Management, Fundraising, and Grant Writing

Prepare and manage annual operating budgets.  
Lead grant writing efforts by identifying funding opportunities, preparing competitive applications, and securing federal, state, local, and private funding to support WPBgo programs.  
Lead fundraising efforts, securing sponsorships, memberships, donations, and other funding sources to support WPBgo’s financial sustainability.  
Oversee grant administration, funding agreements, compliance, and reporting requirements.  
Ensure strong financial accountability, transparency, and compliance with all funding and reporting requirements.  
Develop and implement strategies to expand and diversify WPBgo’s funding to support organizational goals and program growth. 

Stakeholder Engagement

Build and maintain strong relationships with public and private sector partners.  
Advocate for mobility initiatives and funding opportunities  
Represent WPBgo at public meetings, conferences, workshops, and community events.  

Board and Staff Leadership

Partner with the Board of Directors to establish organizational priorities, policies, and strategic initiatives.  
Provide recommendations regarding governance, funding, and organizational growth.  
Recruit, supervise, and develop staff, consultants, and program partners.  
Ensure compliance with all personnel policies, employment regulations, and organizational standards.  
Foster a collaborative and results driven organizational culture.  

Communications and Public Outreach

Lead public awareness, marketing, and community engagement efforts.  
Promote alternative transportation options including transit, ridesharing, biking, walking, micromobility, and mobility services.

Experience working with boards of directors, community stakeholders, government agencies, employers, and funding partners.

Familiarity with Palm Beach County, South Florida transportation agencies, local governments, and regional mobility initiatives.  
Experience working with Metropolitan Planning Organizations, transit agencies, employers, developers, and community organizations.

This position operates in a professional setting with frequent interactions with public officials, business leaders, community stakeholders, and transportation partners. Occasional evening meetings and local travel throughout Palm Beach County and South Florida region may be required.

How to Apply
This is a part-time, independent-contractor (1099) position. To apply, please send a cover letter and resume describing your interest in community arts and this role to jobs@socowomenschorus.org .   

About SoCo Women's Chorus
Founded in 2012, SoCo Women's Chorus (“SoCo”) is an auditioned community treble chorus based in Austin. Since our founding, we've been a welcoming and safe space for women and LGBTQ+ singers, bringing nearly 100 voices together in performances that celebrate artistic excellence, inclusion, and community connection.

Over the past several years, under the leadership of our Artistic Director Lisa Holt, SoCo has grown remarkably—more than doubling in size, significantly expanding its earned and contributed revenue, and earning transformative support through the City of Austin arts funding. As the chorus continues to grow, we are creating our first-ever Executive Director position to help  build the organizational foundation that will carry us into our next chapter.

The Executive Director will partner closely with the Artistic Director and Board of Directors to strengthen operations, support our volunteers and committees, deepen community engagement, and position SoCo for long-term sustainability and success.

Why This Role Matters
This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys building organizations. The Executive Director will play a key role in helping SoCo Women's Chorus transition from a volunteer-operated organization to one supported by professional administrative leadership. Because SoCo is growing quickly, this role blends hands-on operations with organizational building—running the day-to-day while shaping how it gets done. Working alongside an engaged Board of Directors and a GRAMMY® nominated Artistic Director, the Executive Director will help establish systems, strengthen operations, and create the foundation for continued artistic and organizational growth. As SoCo Women's Chorus continues to grow its audience, programs, and financial capacity, there is opportunity for compensation to grow alongside the organization, based on organizational needs, performance, and financial sustainability. 

Key Responsibilities
ORGANIZATIONAL LEADERSHIP

Serve as the organization's primary administrative leader, partnering with the Board and Artistic Director to advance the mission of SoCo Women's Chorus.
Develop organizational systems and processes that will help improve efficiency and sustainability.
Ensure SoCo's critical functions are carried out with consistency and quality, building the clarity and structure needed for durable organizational practice as volunteer and board roles change over time.
Help SoCo continue its ongoing evolution from a working board toward a governing board—architecting the systems, roles, and structure that support that shift as it unfolds.
Support the Board's annual and strategic planning, and take the lead on executing and tracking progress on the organization's operational goals.
Supervise select contractors and any future administrative staff, and partner with the Board and Artistic Director to plan for the staffing that continued growth may require.
Provide regular reports and recommendations to the Board regarding organizational progress, priorities, and operational needs.

CHORUS & PROGRAM OPERATIONS 

Lead the operational planning, logistics, and coordination that bring SoCo's mission to life through our programs, concerts, and community performances, in close partnership with the Artistic Director's creative leadership. 
Oversee SoCo's concert and event production, ensuring performances are polished and professional, and build stronger systems over time—strengthening the Event Production committee and Event Production Manager contractor role to support SoCo's growing slate of performances.
Oversee the Chorus Officers (a volunteer Chorus Management leadership team) who are responsible for the day-to-day running of the chorus, including member communications, registration, logistics, and everything that keeps singers informed, organized, and ready to perform.
Lead and strengthen SoCo's dedicated community of volunteers and committees—ensuring roles are clear, people are well-supported, and everyone has the tools they need to succeed.

FUNDRAISING & DEVELOPMENT
Partner with the Board to shape SoCo's fundraising strategy and define clear roles across the Board, Executive Director, and volunteers.
Coordinate and support the volunteer teams who lead SoCo's signature fundraising initiatives, such as Amplify Austin and the annual silent auction.
Coordinate with SoCo's grants administrator on grant strategy, applications, and reporting.
Help identify new funding opportunities that support the organization's long-term sustainability.

MARKETING & COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT
Own SoCo's marketing strategy and annual communications calendar—strengthening how SoCo is perceived, promoting our concerts and programs, and supporting fundraising and community engagement.
Ensure marketing gets done reliably and on-brand across all channels—such as our website, email, social media, and concert playbills—building the systems and coordinating the mix of volunteers, contractors, and direct work that keep it consistent even as volunteers change.
Grow audience, ticket sales, and playbill ad revenue to strengthen earned income, developing SoCo's reach and building on our audience growth of recent years.
Serve as an enthusiastic ambassador for SoCo in the Austin community, supported by the members, Board, and volunteers who already carry much of this outreach.

ADMINISTRATION & FINANCE
Collaborate with the Treasurer (who leads SoCo's finances with external bookkeeping support) and Board on budgeting and financial oversight. Monitor expenditures across programs and operations to keep spending on budget, working with the Treasurer to anticipate and address variances as they arise.
Bring clear ownership and reliable systems to SoCo's back-office and technology systems—data, records, contracts, etc—building consistent processes where responsibilities have shifted between volunteers and board members over time.
Track and report on SoCo's impact and outcomes to guide program and organizational decisions, strengthen fundraising, and support continuous improvement.
Ensure compliance with organizational policies, required filings, insurance, and grant reporting obligations.

Qualifications
WE’RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO…

Believes in the power of community arts and connects with SoCo's mission.
Is caring, emotionally intelligent, and a supportive team player. Someone who builds trust, navigates change and challenging conversations with professionalism, and supports the people around them.
Is a strategic and systems-thinker who notices what isn't yet owned and helps build the structure to handle it.
Is detail oriented and dependable—meets deadlines and keeps details from slipping through the cracks.
Is a self-starter who takes initiative to move work forward.
Able to balance big-picture strategy with hands-on execution—who is comfortable enhancing  an organization while helping run it.
Communicates clearly in writing and in person.
Is comfortable with budgets and financial oversight, and  can read and understand budgets and financial information with confidence.
Enjoys working with and supporting volunteers, and leads and fosters an environment  that encourages  people to show up to support SoCo’s overall mission.
Bachelor’s degree or higher preferred.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

Nonprofit administration or operations
Arts management
Systems- or process-building in a growing organization
Fundraising and development
Volunteer and committee coordination
Marketing and communications
Grant coordination and reporting
Budgeting and financial management
Familiarity with tools such as QuickBooks, Eventbrite, Mailchimp, Canva, Givebutter, and Squarespace

The Opportunity
This position offers the opportunity to help shape the future of one of Central Texas' fastest-growing community choruses. As the organization continues to expand its artistic impact and community presence, the Executive Director will help build the administrative foundation needed to support and enhance future growth. Because this is SoCo's first Executive Director, this role will evolve over time. The Executive Director will work with the Board and Artistic Director to set priorities, refine responsibilities, and build the practices that support SoCo's continued growth.

Executive Director -
The Arc Connecticut

The Moran Company is pleased to partner with The Arc Connecticut to recruit the organization's Executive Director.

The Arc Connecticut is an advocacy organization committed to protecting the rights of individuals with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (I/DD) and promoting opportunities for their full inclusion in their communities. The organization is the statewide chapter affiliated with The Arc of the United States [https://thearc.org/], the nation's oldest and largest non-profit federation advocating for and supporting people with I/DD and their families since 1950. The Arc Connecticut is an independent 501(c)(3) corporation established in Connecticut over 60 years ago. As the state chapter, The Arc convenes and supports 13 other Arc chapters (independent corporations) with total combined revenue of over $111 million, more than 170 board members, over 4,000 staff, and over 1,800 volunteers.

The Arc Connecticut has grown and adapted to the changes that people with disabilities face across their life span. Through the decades, The Arc has seen several name changes, advocated for the passage of state legislation on behalf of people with disabilities, assisted in the creation of and advocated for the private provider system of support, filed 4 class action lawsuits, advocated for the closure of institutions, and continued to advocate for individuals with I/DD and their families.

The work today is illustrated by The Arc Connecticut Family Network (formerly Families for Families), created in 2012 to give families a united voice — within the Department of Developmental Services (DDS), at the Capitol, and across their local communities. The network brings families together to share information, collaborate on local and statewide issues, and connect directly with lawmakers and Connecticut's federal delegation under the leadership of the Director of Advocacy.

The organization advances its public policy priorities through an annual legislative agenda, supported by family and advocate education, network growth, legislative outreach, relationship-building, coalitions, and partnerships.

The Arc Connecticut is governed by a volunteer board of 16, led by two staff members (including the Executive Director), and supported by annual revenue of $450,000 generated by chapter dues and fundraising. In addition, efforts are amplified through contracts with marketing/public relations consultants and a governmental affairs consultant. The Executive Director position is based within the state of Connecticut, and duties are performed remotely.

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of The Arc Connecticut, leading statewide advocacy and policy efforts while overseeing operations, supporting local chapters, implementing strategic plans, and building relationships

with key stakeholders. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ideal candidate will be an outgoing, visionary, and analytical leader with fundraising experience and knowledge of, or the ability to learn, the funding and service-delivery systems for people with I/DD.

The Executive Director will serve as the organization's primary spokesperson and advocate, advancing policies, programs, and services that benefit individuals with I/DD and their families. This leader will develop and implement the organization's policy and strategic agendas, monitor legislative and regulatory developments, build coalitions, and represent The Arc Connecticut in public policy forums. The Executive Director will support local chapters by providing guidance, training, resources, and opportunities for collaboration while incorporating their priorities into statewide efforts. Responsibilities also include overseeing daily operations, staff, finances, compliance, fundraising, community engagement, and organizational effectiveness. Position Summary

The Greater Idaho Falls Chamber of Commerce seeks a visionary, collaborative, and results-oriented Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead one of Idaho's most influential business organizations. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO serves as the Chamber's chief executive, strategic leader, and public ambassador, advancing a thriving business environment while championing the economic vitality of Greater Idaho Falls.

The ideal candidate possesses an integral understanding of the region's diverse stakeholders and recognizes the extraordinary opportunities that exist across Eastern Idaho. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring both executive vision and operational execution. The successful candidate is equally comfortable in the boardroom, at a legislative meeting, meeting with business owners, or helping execute Chamber events.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership
Develop and execute the Chamber's strategic vision in partnership with the Board of Directors.
Identify opportunities that strengthen the regional economy and enhance the Chamber's value to its members.
Position the Chamber as a respected leader on issues affecting business and community prosperity.

Relationship Building & Community Leadership
Serve as a trusted connector among businesses, elected officials, educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, economic development partners, and community leaders.
Build productive relationships that foster collaboration and long-term regional success.
Represent the Chamber as a credible, nonpartisan, third-party advocate for the business community.

Membership & Business Development
Grow and retain Chamber membership by delivering measurable value.
Engage businesses of all sizes while cultivating strategic partnerships and sponsorships.
Support programs that encourage entrepreneurship, workforce development, and business success.

Organizational Leadership
Lead and develop Chamber staff through effective coaching, accountability, and professional development.
Ensure operational excellence across finance, communications, programming, and member services.
Manage the Chamber's budget and resources with sound financial stewardship.

Governance
Work closely with the Board of Directors to establish priorities, implement policy, and maintain strong governance practices.
Support board development, committee engagement, and volunteer leadership.
Provide timely reporting and recommendations that enable informed decision-making.

Advocacy
Advocate for policies and initiatives that strengthen the regional business climate.
Serve as a respected voice on issues impacting commerce and economic development.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal CEO is a trusted and respected leader who builds credibility through integrity, transparency, and accountability. They serve as a valued connector, bringing together business leaders, elected officials, educators, nonprofit organizations, and community partners to achieve shared goals. With strong business acumen and executive judgment, this individual understands the opportunities and challenges facing organizations of all sizes and consistently makes thoughtful, strategic decisions that support long-term organizational and regional success.

This leader combines visionary thinking with exceptional execution. They are an experienced executive who inspires confidence among staff, volunteer leaders, public officials, and the business community while fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and accountability. They possess a comprehensive management skill set, including financial stewardship, strategic planning, organizational development, talent management, effective communication, change leadership, and conflict resolution.

The successful candidate understands the critical partnership between a chief executive and a governing board. They have experience working effectively with volunteer leadership, respect the distinct roles of governance and management, and cultivate strong, productive relationships that support sound decision-making and organizational success. As the public face of the Chamber, the CEO serves as a credible, nonpartisan advocate for the business community, representing the collective interests of Chamber members with professionalism and objectivity.

Above all, the ideal candidate is equally comfortable shaping long-term vision and delivering day-to-day results, leading by example through active participation in Chamber programs, member engagement, community events, legislative advocacy, fundraising, and organizational operations. They understand that exceptional Chamber leadership requires visibility, accessibility, and a genuine commitment to serving the business community.

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Yachad, a division of The Orthodox Union, the nation’s largest Orthodox Jewish organization‚ supports individuals with intellectual, developmental, and learning disabilities. Yachad helps these individuals participate more fully in Jewish life and the broader society by providing educational, employment and relationship opportunities.

The Orthodox Union (OU) is the largest Orthodox Jewish organization in the U.S., founded in 1898. The OU supports a vast network of synagogues, youth programs, advocacy efforts, services for individuals with disabilities, and international initiatives. It also operates the leading kosher certification service, recognized globally by the Ⓤ symbol on numerous kosher food products.

More About Yachad:

Operates the largest stand-alone Jewish special education school system (IVDU), which currently operates 4 schools in New York and New Jersey, educating 150 students annually.
Operates adult day programs currently in New York and New Jersey, with a focus on helping individuals develop skills and opportunities to contribute to the community.
As a summer camp/program provider, provides more diverse opportunities for more participants than any Jewish provider of summer experiences for individuals with disabilities. These include inclusive camp experiences, vocational experiences, travel programs, vacation style programs, and include both single gender and co-educational options.
Operates 10 regions serving over 20 communities providing social and relationship opportunities through weekday evening programs, Shabbatonim, and much more. More than 1000 individuals participate in these programs annually.
Began the first of its kind resource and referral service (REACH) that is data informed, and completely free. Families from around the world can call to speak with a qualified professional and receive referrals from our vast database.
Engages youth, both school aged and college aged students in helping to desensitize attitudes towards individuals with disabilities, as well as encourage volunteerism and service in our youth.

Position Summary:

Yachad is seeking a relationship-driven and strategic Director of Development to lead fundraising efforts in our fastest-growing region, Yachad South Florida.

The Director of Development is responsible for the identification, cultivation, stewardship, and solicitation of charitable gifts from existing and new donors. This position is responsible for cultivating and maintaining relationships with key community members to strengthen Yachad’s fundraising capabilities.

Responsibilities:

Develop and manage a portfolio of fundraising donors and prospects through all phases of the giving cycle, from validation and engagement through cultivation, solicitation, gift negotiation, and stewardship with the expectation of growing the campaign to a minimum of $500K annually.
Conduct a minimum of 60 prospect meetings annually to cultivate and solicit prospects and close gifts.
Complete a minimum of 30 major gift solicitations annually.
Plan and organize fundraising events to help fulfill fundraising goals.
Work in partnership with the Regional Director to identify key prospects and leaders who will move Yachad South Florida’s fundraising forward.
Responsible for managing communications and follow-up, including detailed contact reports on all donor prospects in portfolio and updating all moves in Yachad’s CRM, Velocity.
Perform additional duties and responsibilities as needed.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent required
A minimum of 7 years of fundraising or related transferable experience required.
Strong commitment to Jewish philanthropy and serving the disability community.
Experience presenting priorities and presenting information clearly and compellingly, both in writing and in person.
Previous demonstrated experience successfully closing 5- and 6-figure gifts.
Strong knowledge of the philanthropic Jewish community in Florida is essential.
Highly motivated self-starter who can work independently and as part of a team.
Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing an annual campaign strategy.

Salary and Benefits:

This position has a competitive salary, commensurate with experience.

Health, Dental & Vision Insurance:

The OU offers health insurance through an Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement (ICHRA). Instead of a single group plan, employees have the freedom to choose their own health insurance plan that fits their personal and family needs. The OU contributes a generous monthly amount directly toward your premium, making coverage more flexible, affordable, and tailored to you.

Employees enrolled in our health plan also receive an annual BeniComp stipend, a supplemental benefit that reimburses eligible medical, pharmaceutical, dental, and vision expenses.

In addition, the OU offers employees group dental and vision insurance through MetLife.

Additional Benefits and Perks:

10 paid sick days
10-15 paid vacation days
Paid Jewish and Federal holidays
Short Fridays to accommodate for Sabbath observance
Free life and disability insurance
Discounted continuing education opportunities
403(b) retirement plan with a 5% employer match after 3 years (requires a minimum 2% employee contribution)
