Managing Director – Texas

Overview:

VIOTAS is seeking a Managing Director to lead its Texas business. This is a senior leadership appointment at a fast-scaling, technology-driven energy company, and an opportunity to lead an established and growing operation in one of the world’s most dynamic electricity markets.
VIOTAS operates at the leading edge of the demand response industry, enabling large commercial, industrial, and data centre customers to participate actively in the ERCOT market — generating revenue for those customers while supporting grid reliability and the integration of renewable energy. The Texas business is built on proprietary technology, deep international market expertise, and a growing local team, supported by specialist functions from the global organisation.
A particular area of opportunity is the large and fast-growing data centre sector. VIOTAS brings market-leading power quality intelligence, fault ride-through, and grid-compliance capability that help large energy users and data centres meet ERCOT’s technical and operational requirements — supporting faster interconnection and compliant operation as the Texas grid framework evolves. Building VIOTAS’s position in this segment is a significant part of the opportunity for the incoming Managing Director.

About VIOTAS:

Established in Limerick, Ireland in 2013, VIOTAS set about designing and delivering new innovations to address the challenges posed by increased renewable generation in electrical grids: How can a grid be balanced when a large amount of electricity is coming from unpredictable renewable sources that are difficult to forecast and that change the fundamental principles of how grids operate?
In response, VIOTAS developed proprietary technologies that place electricity customers at the core of the solution. By managing their electricity consumption and onsite generation in real-time, VIOTAS help balance the wider electricity grid. The company then aggregates participating customers to form Virtual Power Plants which are traded in the electricity market, competing against conventional fossil fuel power stations. This approach not only generates significant revenue for participating customers but also contributes to reducing carbon emissions. With a global expansion strategy, VIOTAS, currently with over 110 staff, operates in Ireland, Poland, USA and Australia.

The Role

Lead the Texas business end to end — owning the market P&L and accountable for revenue, growth, and the overall performance of the operation.
Drive commercial growth, acquiring and retaining large energy customers and securing strategic partnerships across the Texas market.
Lead the operational performance of the Texas business, ensuring VIOTAS’s technology and services are deployed and delivered to the highest standards of reliability and compliance.
Hold a deep, current understanding of the ERCOT market — nodal dynamics, ancillary services, interconnection, and the regulatory and policy trajectory — and position the business to capture the value that market creates.
Represent VIOTAS at the senior level with ERCOT, the PUCT, utilities, policymakers, customers, and industry bodies, and build the company’s profile and influence in the Texas energy market.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing local team, and set a results-driven, customer-focused culture.
Provide regular operational, commercial and financial reporting to the VIOTAS Board and Senior Leadership Team.
Ensure the Texas business operates in compliance with all applicable legal, regulatory and corporate governance requirements.
Collaborate closely with the global leadership team to align market strategy, product development priorities and organisational goals.

What We’re Looking For

A proven senior leader with a track record of running a business or a substantial market operation, with full accountability for commercial and operational performance.
Strong commercial and financial acumen, with experience owning a P&L and delivering against revenue and growth targets.
Deep knowledge of the ERCOT market — market rules, demand response and ancillary service mechanisms, and grid services — with the intellectual appetite to hold that knowledge as a continuous working discipline, not a static credential.
An established network across the Texas energy sector — ERCOT, the PUCT, utilities, and large energy users — or a clear and credible pathway to building one quickly.
The ability to translate market and regulatory direction into commercial and operational positioning, and to set the strategy that follows from it.
Genuine leadership ability — building and developing a team, and delivering through others rather than through personal effort alone.
Excellent communication and representation skills, with the credibility to speak for VIOTAS to customers, regulators, and the wider market.
An entrepreneurial, ownership mindset, comfortable operating with autonomy in a fast-growing international business.
Awareness of the power reliability, resilience, and grid-compliance challenges facing large energy users and data centres in the ERCOT market is an advantage.

Competitive executive package, including base salary, performance bonus, participation in the company Management Share Incentive Plan, and benefits, commensurate with experience.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
The Director of Development serves as the strategic leader of all fundraising and philanthropic initiatives for Community Storehouse. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, this position is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive fundraising strategy that ensures the organization's long-term financial sustainability and supports its mission of serving children and families in our community.
About Christian Community Storehouse, Inc Our underserved communities are continuing to grow and are forever changing. At the Community Storehouse, our mission and focus have been and will continue to be on the needs of our children. Increasingly however, it is becoming entire families that we serve too. As a result, we are evolving to address these and other challenges systematically. We seek to grow and develop sustainable public and private partnerships, where jointly, we develop solutions and ways to serve more people together, since no single organization can do this work alone. By creating collaborative partnerships that thrive, we can create limitless possibilities and additional resources for underserved children, their families, and the communities at large.
Description The Director of Development cultivates meaningful relationships with donors, corporate partners, foundations, and community leaders while leading a high-performing development team. This role is responsible for growing philanthropic revenue through diversified funding sources, strengthening donor engagement, increasing community awareness, and advancing Community Storehouse's strategic priorities.

Essential Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Partner with the CEO to establish annual fundraising goals aligned with the organization's strategic plan and operating budget.
Develop, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive annual Development Plan that supports both current operations and future growth.
Create long-term fundraising strategies that include:
Major Gifts
Annual Giving
Corporate Partnerships
Foundation Giving
Capital Campaigns
Planned Giving
Special Events
Sponsorship Development
Identify emerging fundraising trends and implement innovative strategies that strengthen organizational sustainability.
Serve as a key member of the leadership team, contributing to organizational planning and decision-making.

Donor Relations & Fundraising

Build, cultivate, solicit, and steward a portfolio of major donors and prospective donors.
Develop and execute comprehensive donor stewardship and communication plans that demonstrate the impact of philanthropic investments.
Inspire and motivate individuals, businesses, foundations, and community partners to invest in the mission of Community Storehouse.
Manage and expand corporate giving and sponsorship opportunities.
Identify and pursue new funding opportunities, including grants and collaborative partnerships.
Ensure timely donor recognition and meaningful stewardship activities.

Community Engagement

Serve as an ambassador for Community Storehouse throughout the community.
Develop and maintain strategic relationships with local businesses, civic organizations, schools, churches, foundations, and community leaders.
Represent the organization at community events, networking functions, chambers of commerce, Rotary clubs, women's organizations, and other civic groups.
Secure speaking engagements and cultivate opportunities to increase visibility and community support.
Collaborate with the marketing and communications team to promote fundraising campaigns, organizational impact, newsletters, social media, and donor communications.

Leadership & Team Management

Lead, mentor, and develop the Development Department, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, and excellence.
Directly supervise the Development Manager and provide strategic oversight of fundraising events.
Recruit, train, and evaluate development and public relations staff as needed.
Collaborate across departments to ensure fundraising initiatives align with organizational priorities and program needs.

Financial Management & Reporting

Develop and manage the annual Development Department budget.
Participate as an active member of the Finance Committee.
Monitor fundraising performance through data analysis, donor metrics, and key performance indicators.
Prepare regular reports for the CEO, Board of Directors, and Development Committee regarding fundraising progress, campaign effectiveness, donor retention, and revenue projections.
Ensure accurate donor records and effective utilization of the donor database.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in Business, Communications, Marketing, Nonprofit Management, or a related field.
Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional fundraising experience with a demonstrated record of increasing philanthropic revenue.
Proven success managing and growing a comprehensive development program.
Experience cultivating and soliciting major gifts.
Exceptional relationship-building, interpersonal, and communication skills.
Strong organizational, leadership, and strategic planning abilities.
Experience developing and managing departmental budgets.
Ability to manage multiple priorities while meeting deadlines.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and donor management software (CRM).

Preferred

Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) credential.
Experience with grant writing and foundation relations.
Knowledge of Google Ad Grants and basic graphic design platforms such as Canva or Adobe Creative Suite.
Experience managing fundraising campaigns and nonprofit marketing initiatives.
Experience working with nonprofit boards and volunteer leadership.

Core Competencies

Strategic Leadership
Relationship Management
Major Gift Fundraising
Donor Stewardship
Team Leadership
Financial Acumen
Public Speaking
Project Management
Collaboration
Communication
Integrity and Accountability

Success Measures

Success in this role will be demonstrated by but no limited too:

Achievement or exceeding of annual fundraising goals.
Growth in major donor giving and donor retention.
Increased corporate partnerships and sponsorship revenue.
Expansion of foundation and grant funding.
Successful execution of fundraising campaigns and special events.
Strengthened community visibility and engagement.
Development of a highly effective and collaborative fundraising team.

Salary $70,000 - $75,000 per year

new_jobs.title: Deputy Director - Department of County Human Services (DCHS)
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

Overview

Multnomah County
is seeking a Department of County Human Services (DCHS) Deputy Director
that will be responsible for assisting the Department Director with the leadership, vision, direction and accountability for activities and operations of the department’s divisions. You will assist the Director in leading a dedicated workforce of approximately 1,140 employees, currently organized into four main divisions, and manage a budget of approximately $559 million. This position provides support to the Department Director and the four Divisions of DCHS: Aging, Disability, and Veterans Services; Intellectual and Development Disabilities Services; Youth and Family Services; and Preschool and Early Learning. This position also provides support to the areas of Business Services, Human Resources, and the Director’s Office. It directs the daily administrative operations of the department and leads day-to-day functions, the Strategic Engagement Team (SET), Trauma Informed Practice, Emergency Management & Mass Care Coordination, and any other functions as assigned by the Department Director. It provides leadership and policy direction as DCHS liaison to Central County services such as IT, Facilities, Talent Development, Privacy/HIPAA, Government Relations and Communications.

Department Administration

Direct the daily business and administrative operations of the department by managing and coordinating operational activities and leading day-to-day functions that are carried out by the DCHS divisions, as assigned by the department director.
Provide leadership and policy direction as DCHS liaison to central County services such as IT, Facilities, Fleet, Records, Communications, Distribution services and others.
Participates in committees both internal and external as the DCHS Director's representative.
Direct the daily administrative operations of the department and lead day-to-day functions performed by Performance and Data Management, The Strategic Engagement Team (SET), Trauma Informed Practice, Emergency Management, and any other functions as assigned by the department director.
Direct the centralized leadership for emergency preparedness, severe weather response, and federal action emergency activations.
Oversee the execution of Mass Care (Emergency Support Function 6 / ESF-6) services, including shelter, food, water, and life-safety distribution systems for unhoused and vulnerable populations.
Ensure the Department Strategic Plan is embedded and implemented across each Division and intersects with the Countywide Strategic Plan.

Budget Administration

Provide oversight and direction in the development, administration and ongoing management of the DCHS $559 million budget in partnership with the Department Director and Finance Director.
Provide policy direction for determining priorities for the department in contracted services and staffing.
Review, monitor and approve expenditures in partnership with the Finance Director.
Implement related budget modifications.
Serves as Departmental management liaison to the DCHS Citizen Budget Advisory Committee.

Department Leadership

Guide internal teams to engage in department-wide high priority initiatives and work collaboratively with senior leaders to identify process improvement opportunities addressing efficiency, effectiveness, customer focus, data driven and with equity lens.
Guide and provide oversight to ensure enterprise-wide initiatives are realistically scoped, fiscally responsible and operationally sustainable.
Oversee and implement the department’s Strategic Plan and framework to align with the DCHS North Star, the DCHS Work Force Equity Strategic Plan and the County's Strategic Plan and mission and equity goals.
Work with division leadership to identify mission critical initiatives and priorities that central services can support.
Establish a multi-dimensional approach to delivering services and achieving mission using Quality Improvement tools, Innovation practices, Equity centered, and Human centered Design and research.
Designs, aligns, and evaluates cross-divisional human-centered service systems across the Department of County Human Services (DCHS); Guides programmatic equity and innovation for core divisions; Leads programmatic and funding alignment across the Department.
Provide leadership and oversight for all special projects that come from the Board of Commissioners and the Chair’s Office.
Provide executive direction over the centralized Data and Evaluation Services team to improve transparency, track outcome metrics, and advance continuous quality improvement. Oversee research designs, gap analyses, and community-centered evaluations (e.g., Decline Studies, focus groups) to align program hours and services with family preferences.

Finance and Personnel Management

Create and support talent management strategies to support diversity and backfill requirements.
Develop department-wide staff performance management that ties to department goals and its strategic plan.
Assist Department Director in reviewing recruitment strategies and processes.
Develop grant/foundation strategy for each fiscal year.
Oversee the Leadership development and training initiative for the department.
Provide oversight and policy direction for DCHS fiscal systems development and planning. Lead, coordinate and participate in the development of departmental work plans, strategic plans, goals and objectives.
Direct and approve through subordinate managers the planning, prioritizing, assigning, supervising, training, review, and the daily administrative and transactional business workflows of the department, ensuring strict compliance with all County procurement and contracting policies. Act as a resource, and provide direction, guidance, and leadership to staff; advise on the more complex and sensitive concerns and issues; may select, direct, and manage the work of consultants.
Develop, administer, assist, and monitor budgets in partnership with the Finance Director; develop justifications for budgetary recommendations and/or adjustments; participate in forecasting additional funds for staffing and resources; identify, obtain, and manage funding from grants and community partners; participate in the interpretation, negotiation, management, and enforcement of contracts; coordinate the finalization of budgets to ensure timely submission of the department budget.

Equity, Partnerships & Innovation

Apply an equity lens to all decision-making, actively identifying and dismantling policies and practices that create unnecessary barriers and perpetuate unlawful discrimination.
Enforce policies that protect marginalized employees and ensure equitable service delivery for the community.
Cultivate deep partnerships with specialized housing providers and advocacy groups to design and implement residential programs that specifically support individuals with diverse needs.
Strengthen data privacy to ensure DCHS safeguards client information.
Cultivate deep partnerships with city officials, school districts, and community groups to create a functional system of care.
Develop and conceptualize new enterprises or joint ventures among various agencies, both internal and external to the County, to create innovative, or more efficient or effective services.
Innovate internal policies and practices to ensure strong financial stewardship of public funds, contracts, and resources.
Serve as a primary liaison and authorized representative for DCHS to public officials, Board Commissioners, government relations bodies, and media outlets.

Minimum Qualifications/Transferable Skills:

A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent related work experience
Minimum of 6 years of increasingly responsible professional experience in Human Services
Minimum of 6 years experience managing and working in a public sector unionized (represented) environment.

Preferred Qualifications/Transferable Skills: You do not need to have the following preferred qualifications/transferable skills to qualify. However, keep in mind we may consider some or all of the following when identifying the most qualified candidates. Please clearly explain on your application how you meet any of the following preferred qualifications/transferable skills.

Master’s Degree
6 years of Experience in Senior Level role focused on Human Services
Substantial experience in budget planning, financial management, and resource optimization. Examples include managing multi-million dollar (i.e., $300 Million +) departmental budgets, forecasting personnel costs, and overseeing capital expenditures.
Public Sector/Governmental Experience: Direct, substantial experience in a large county (i.e., 5,000 + employees), state, or municipal government or other comparable complex public-sector entity.
Demonstrated experience communicating complex human capital strategies and organizational data clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences, ranging from frontline employees and union representatives to executive leadership and the Board of Commissioners
Experience in promoting a culture of respect, inclusiveness, and appreciation of diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and values.
